content:
incident-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT: Prod runtime latency spike detected after 23:15 deploy. Auto-alerting teams. Metrics: p95=1.6s (normal 0.25s), throughput -20%.

alex: I'm oncall. getting paged now — investigating. Which release rolled?

deploy-bot: Release 2026.03.15.r42 deployed to canary @ 23:12, promoted to 30% at 23:20, 100% at 23:25. Canary showed elevated p95 at ~23:18.

mike: seeing kernel selector fallbacks in logs — many nodes reporting `kernel=generic-fallback` after OOM-triggered evictions.

sara: Confirmed. From the runtime logs:
```
2026-03-15T23:26:10Z host-12 runtime WARN kernel_select: fallback to generic-kernel, reason=kernel_init_timeout
2026-03-15T23:26:11Z host-14 kvcache ERROR failed_retain: eviction-loop
```

alex: Customer impact? CS?

jen: CS: small but growing set of customers (prod-chat, docs-search) reporting slow responses and occasional 503s. No large-scale outage yet, but SLA KPIs trending down. I'm prepping customer comms.

alex: Immediate plan — 1) throttle rollout to 0% (kill-switch flag) 2) if needed, rollback to previous build 3) shift critical traffic to dedicated pool. Sara, can you toggle the selector flag?

sara: Toggling `runtime_kernel_selector_v2` -> off now. Command run: `./ffctl set runtime_kernel_selector_v2 false --env prod`

ops-bot: featureflag: runtime_kernel_selector_v2 set to false by sara at 2026-03-15T23:32:05Z

mike: after flag flip, p95 dropped from 1.6s -> 0.6s in 2m, throughput still -8%. We're seeing reduced kernel fallbacks but batching tail-latency increased (microbatch flush delays).

alex: Good. Let's hold the kill-switch at off. If throughput doesn't recover to < -5% within 10m, initiate rollback. Who can run rollback?

mike: I'm starting rollback to 2026.03.10.r39 now on staging, will promote to prod if health checks pass. Rolling back canary first.

deploy-bot: Rollback job started: rollback:2026.03.10.r39 -> canary at 23:41. Health-checks in progress.

jen: Notifying affected customers with a brief note: "We've detected increased latency following a recent deploy and are actively mitigating. We'll update within 30 minutes."

sara: Observability: tracing shows request QPS distribution shifting -> more long tail on specific model routes (/chat/generate). Suspect batching + kernel mismatch. Dumping batcher stats: `batch_wait_avg=35ms -> 210ms` on slice-9.

mike: Confirmed rollback to canary succeeded at 23:47. Metrics: canary p95=0.28s, throughput back to -2%. Promoting rollback to 100% in 1m.

deploy-bot: Promote rollback started at 23:48. Full prod revert completed at 23:51.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigation applied. status=mitigated, mitigation=rollback+flag_off, started=23:32, resolved=23:51.

alex: Handing to eng-sre for post-incident analysis. Key actions: preserve logs (hosts 12/14/19), collect batcher traces, kernel selector telemetry, and reproduce failure under load in staging.

mike: I'll capture heap/kv metrics and run a targeted stress job on the thinslice path.

jen: CS will follow up with impacted customers with root-cause summary and ETA for RCA.

sara: Creating incident ticket and assigning to eng-runtime for RCA. prelim hypothesis: kernel selector v2 has edge case leading to init timeouts under a specific memory pressure pattern which triggers fallback -> increased eviction -> batching stalls.

alex: Thanks team. If anything regresses, re-open this thread. We'll sync tomorrow 10:00 for RCA review. :thumbsup:
